data.text: [00:00]CD1 Track 21
T = Tarin, M = Marcos
[00:04]Hi Marcos, what are you doing next Thursday? `[00:08]And your brother too ... is he around?
[00:11.6]Erm ... next Thursday? `[00:14]Ermm ... my brother is staying with friends next week ... but I’m not doing anything. Why?
[00:22]Well, I’m having a meal at my house to celebrate Thanksgiving and I’d really like you to come.
[00:29.6]Oh, thanks, I’d love to! `[00:32]That’s very kind of you! I’ve never been to a Thanksgiving meal before. … `[00:38]It’s an important festival here, isn’t it?

[00:41]Yes, and I’m going to cook roast turkey! `[00:45]Thanksgiving is all about the food ... well, ... really just getting together with family and friends and having a lovely meal. `[00:54]Sometimes, after the meal, people go out for a walk or something, but mostly, they just sit around and watch TV together.
[01:01]Mmm ... and what about presents and things? `[01:05]Is it a time when you give presents to people, like at Christmas or ... ?

[01:10]Ermm ... no, not really... it’s a really big and important celebration but it isn’t commercial. `[01:18]People don’t usually buy lots of presents or anything. `[01:21.8]There are some big public celebrations – like the Macy’s parade in New York. `[01:27]But for most people, it’s just a time for giving thanks, and getting together with family and friends and eating turkey!
[01:34.5]Mmm ... I love roast turkey!

[01:37.3]Yeah, me too. `[01:39]Traditionally, we have roast turkey as the main part of the meal, ... and then there are lots of other dishes. `[01:46.5]I mean, basically, there are four other essential parts to the meal ... sometimes more than four ...
[01:54.5]Really...?

[01:55]Mmm. There are lots of variations too – it depends on where you come from in the States. `[02:02]I’m from the north east and one of the things we have is sweet potatoes with maple syrup. `[02:08.5]It’s very sweet, and some people don’t like it ... but I love it!
[02:13.9]Mm ... I think it sounds delicious ... sweet potatoes and maple syrup ... mmm.

[02:20.8]Yeah ... some people have sweet potatoes baked in the oven – in a sort of pie – but we usually have them boiled ... and then mashed up and ... then with maple syrup on top. `[02:33]Not everyone has maple syrup – in some parts of the States they have sweet potatoes with fresh fruit – things like apples, oranges and pears.
[02:43.3]Really? `[02:44.4]Mmm ... interesting!
[02:46]The second thing we always have is cranberry sauce. `[02:50.7]Have you ever had that?
[02:52]Cranberry sauce? `[02:54.4]No, I don’t think so...
[02:56.6]It goes really well with turkey – it’s made of small red berries – it’s also very sweet actually ... . `[03:04.9]Not everything we have is sweet though! There are some savoury dishes!
[03:10]What else then?
[03:11.8]Well, stuffing is really important. `[03:15.2]I love it ... it’s one of my favourite parts of the meal.
[03:18.7]Stuffing ... ? `[03:20]What’s that?
[03:22]It’s made of bread and meat ... sausages usually – all mixed up together ... and it’s often very spicy!
[03:30.8]Mmm ... so, ... there are basically four other dishes ... what was it? `[03:37]... Sweet potatoes, ... cranberry sauce ... and stuffing ... . What’s the fourth one?
[03:45.4]Well, apple pie of course!
[03:47.7]Aah yes ... I’ve heard about traditional American apple pie.

[03:53]Actually, some people don’t have apple pie. `[03:55.5]In some places, they have pumpkin pie ... or pie made of pecan nuts, which is very popular. `[04:02.8]But in our house, we have apple pie … baked in the oven – it’s fantastic!
[04:07.5]Mmm ... I’m getting hungry just thinking about it all. `[04:11]So, is there anything I can bring?

[04:14.4]Oh, no! Don’t worry about that. `[04:16]Just come and enjoy yourself. `[04:18]We’re eating at about two o’clock in the afternoon – so why don’t you come at about midday for some drinks first?
[04:26]Perfect! `[04:27]See you then ... I’m really looking forward to it ...
